# Conformance corpus

The golden-file corpus for Sherd's Markdown dialect. `QA-002` calls this "the
single highest-value test asset" — build it first, grow it with every bug.

**The harness is not here.** It lives in `internal/conformance/`, because the Go
tool ignores any directory named `testdata` and no test can run inside one.

```sh
go test ./internal/conformance/...
```

The full format is documented in [`docs/formats/conformance.md`](../../docs/formats/conformance.md).

## Two sources

### `commonmark/` — the vendored reference suite

`spec.json`, 652 cases from CommonMark 0.31.2, read **unmodified**. Supplies
Markdown and expected HTML, so these cases exercise HTML comparison only.
`FR-MD-001` requires all 652 to pass.

CC-BY-SA 4.0, © 2014–2016 John MacFarlane. Do not edit it — see
[`commonmark/PROVENANCE.md`](commonmark/PROVENANCE.md).

### `sherd/` — hand-written cases for our own syntax

One directory per case:

```
sherd/<category>/<case-name>/
├── input.md          required
├── output.html       optional — expected rendered HTML
├── ast.json          optional — expected AST, byte ranges mandatory
└── metadata.json     optional — expected links, tags, properties, …
```

A case runs whichever comparisons it provides. An absent file asserts nothing;
an empty array (`"links": []`) asserts emptiness — which is how the
code-precedence cases prove that extended syntax stays inert.

**Current state: a skeleton, not the corpus.** 15 cases covering one example
per extension, enough to prove the layout and give P0.3 a pattern to copy. The
target is ≥ 500 Sherd cases by the end of P0.3.

## Rules

- **A parser change grows the corpus in the same commit.** Not the next one.
- **Every fixed bug adds a case that fails before the fix** (`QA-012`).
- Cases are hand-written or generated by Sherd — never copied from another
  project's suite. The vendored CommonMark suite is the sole exception, and it
  is licensed for it.
- No real personal notes; fixtures are synthetic.
- No third-party branding (`LEG-003`).

## Priority area

Code precedence is the most valuable thing in here. Extended syntax must be
inert inside inline code, fenced code, indented code, and math (`FR-MD-028`) —
the specification flags this as the single most common bug class in this
application category. `sherd/code-precedence/` currently holds three cases; it
should end up holding every extension × every code context.
